source.author: Shelagh Lewins, "Tablet weaving for Dark Age re-enactors"
source.weaveStructure: Threaded-in / warp-twined — all 10 tablets turn forward together every pick; not double-face, not brocade, not twill.
context: The band this pattern reproduces comes from the Oseberg ship burial, Vestfold, Norway, c. 834 AD.
10 tablets. The source page grades this pattern 'A' — 'an accurate copy of a specific band'.
rejectedSources: https://tabletweaving.shelaghlewins.com/ (the URL originally suggested) does not resolve (ENOTFOUND); the working site is https://www.shelaghlewins.com/tablet_weaving/.

GTT's own pattern archive (https://www.guntram.co.za/tabletweaving/patterns/patterns.html) and its threaded-in sub-pages link only to downloadable proprietary .gtt binary files or zipped images, with no page giving both an inline threading/turning chart and a readable resulting band together — it could not be transcribed with confidence and was not used.
transcription: Card colours and S/Z threading were transcribed pixel-by-pixel from the PDF's Figure 6 threading chart, a vector diagram, not a photo, by extracting the embedded images with PyMuPDF and programmatically sampling each cell-centre pixel of the 10x4 grid.

Figure 6's S/Z row labels exist only inside that embedded raster image; the PDF has no separate text-layer copy of them, so they were read directly off the image (once at initial resolution, once after cropping and 6x zoom) rather than confirmed against machine-readable text.

The 8-pick colour sequence was derived from the document's own rotation diagrams (Figure 3: position labelling; Figure 4: which physical hole moves to which position on a forward turn) plus the explicit instruction wording 'turn ... and pass the weft' (turn happens before the weft that becomes a pick, i.e. pick 1 is read after the first turn) — not by running this library's code.
crossChecks: Agrees independently with the PDF's prose description: 'Tablets 1-3 and 9-10: four yellow'; 'Tablets 4, 8: four blue'; 'Tablets 5, 7: one blue, three yellow'; 'Tablet 6: alternating blue and yellow'.
Agrees with the explicit setup instructions: 'turn tablet 5 so the blue thread is in position A'; 'tablet 6 ... positions B and D'; 'tablet 7 ... position C'.

Cross-checked qualitatively against the woven-band photograph (Figure 1): the photo shows a period-4 zigzag running mid-tablet, outer-tablet, mid-tablet, opposite-outer-tablet, matching the derived sequence's column-6/7/6/5 oscillation, with a measured pixel period of ~59px for 4 picks, consistent with the plateau widths seen at the start of the photographed run.
confidence: High for the card setup: an unambiguous vector chart, triple-confirmed against two independent pieces of prose and the setup instructions.

High but not absolute for the pick-to-rotation phase alignment: it rests on the document's diagrams and wording rather than the photo, since a mirrored photo would look identical either way — the photo confirms shape and period, not absolute phase.

meta.name: Narrow Oseberg Band
meta.author: Transcribed from Shelagh Lewins, "Tablet weaving for Dark Age re-enactors"
meta.notes: 10 tablets, silk in the original (rendered here as two colours); all tablets turn forward every pick, no direction reversals within these 8 picks.
